routes.label: in person at the National Identity Card Office

note: Tonga's recognised legal identity is the national identity card: under the National Identity Card Act (2010, revised 2020) every resident must hold one, applying in person at the National Identity Card Office with a birth certificate, photograph and fingerprints (the SEAP digital ID overview). The Act's schedule of fees couldn't be read (PacLII refuses this client), so the fee, the card's term and the time are null.

sources.title: Institute on Statelessness and Inclusion / SEAP, Digital ID overview: Tonga
sources.said: The recognized legal identity in Tonga is the national ID card. ... A birth certificate is required to register for a national ID card. ... , revised in 2020, all residents must possess a national ID card. ... To receive a national ID card, a resident must apply in person at the National Identity Card Office and provide a photograph, fingerprints and other biometric information “if so required”.
